Jordan — attaching the subprocessor export as requested and providing a high-level summary here. If you need an expanded field-by-field export we can produce that under NDA.

Attachment: Redwood-Subprocessors-20270812.csv

Summary (current as of 2027-08-12):
- AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) — Purpose: Core inference serving, S3/EBS storage for model artifacts and runtime caches; Data types: encrypted application data, metadata; Customer content: Yes (encrypted in transit and at rest); Location: US regions; Notes: KMS-managed keys, CMK optional for Dedicated customers.
- GCP (europe-west1) — Purpose: EU-region hosting for EU customers; Data types: same as above; Customer content: Yes; Location: EU.
- Datadog — Purpose: Monitoring/metrics; Data types: metrics and redacted logs; Customer content: No PII (we redact request payloads before sending); Retention: 90 days.
- Sentry — Purpose: error reporting; Data types: stack traces and error metadata; Customer content: No PII by default; Retention: 30 days.
- Managed Backups (ObjectStore Backup Co.) — Purpose: cold backups of model artifacts and telemetry (configurable); Data types: model artifacts, non-PII telemetry; Access: Vendor has encrypted copies for restore only; Location: region-matched.
- Segment (analytics) — Purpose: product analytics; Data types: event metadata (only used if customer enables analytics); Customer content: customers opt-in; Retention: configurable.

Additional notes:
- We do not send raw user message payloads to third-party analytics or error tracking. Any logging that could contain user content is scrubbed/redacted before export.
- Cross-region replication: only for dedicated/enterprise customers when explicitly enabled; standard hosted accounts do not replicate customer data outside the requested region.
- Encryption: all storage is encrypted at rest with provider-managed KMS by default; we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private.

Links: SOC 2 report (redacted) — https://drive.google.com/redwood/soc2-report-202706.pdf 
BAA template — https://drive.google.com/redwood/baa-template.docx

If you want a breakdown in CSV columns (name,purpose,data_types,customer_content,hosting_regions,retention_kv) we included Redwood-Subprocessors-20270812.csv as the export. Please confirm receipt and let us know if any of Acme's security team needs a short 30-min technical Q&A with Dev/ops.

Thanks,
